# KM-160 — CI repair pass 1 (after deletions)

**Lane:** platform · **Complexity:** 2 · **Model:** codex · **Depends on:** KM-124 · **Serializes with:** none (it may touch any file; keep each fix minimal)
**Plan context (pinned):** [M1 plan](https://github.com/aiur-team/khala/blob/reset/m1-external-plan/docs/plans/2026-10-01-002-refactor-external-m1-thin-path-plan.md) · [contracts](https://github.com/aiur-team/khala/blob/reset/m1-external-plan/docs/build/m1/contracts.md) · [roster and graph](https://github.com/aiur-team/khala/blob/reset/m1-external-plan/docs/build/m1/roster.md)
**Exclusive write surfaces:** none exclusive. The surface is whatever the failing CI steps on `main` point at, at pickup.

## Outcome

The `CI` workflow's `validate` job is green on a PR based on the current `main`. This ticket **waits for CI**: the worker watches the PR's CI run to completion and iterates until it is green, without weakening any test. When the PR merges, `main` is green for the SHA it was based on.

## Context and evidence

- KTD11: CI does not gate merges. Reviewers merge with admin override after review, and "a CI-fix ticket runs every few merges" (operator directive, 2026-10-02). This is the first pass, after the big cut (KM-102, KM-120, KM-123 and KM-124).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on `push` to `main` and on PRs (`:8-10`). Job `validate` (`:22-69`) runs these steps:
  1. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`;
  2. `pnpm typecheck`;
  3. `pnpm lint`;
  4. the Chromium install;
  5. `pnpm test`;
  6. Browser tests (`pnpm test:browser`);
  7. Visual baselines (two passes of `@khala/web test:visual` inside `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.63.0-noble`, then `git diff --exit-code -- apps/web/src`);
  8. `pnpm build`.

  KM-102 and KM-124 removed the internal, setup, installed-delivery and recovery steps.
- `.github/workflows/deletion-guard.yml` is a required check that fails when a PR removes files, unless an admin approves the exact head SHA.

## Scope

Every failing step of the most recent completed `CI` run on `main` at pickup (record its run ID and head SHA), plus any further failure the fix PR's own CI run surfaces in those same steps.

## Non-goals

- Failures introduced by merges after the pickup SHA. List them in the PR body; **KM-161** or the next pass owns them.
- Feature work, refactors and dependency upgrades, unless a failure cannot be fixed otherwise (see Risks).
- Live tests that need the KM-101 stack. They are not CI gates (plan Verification Contract).
- Changing branch protection or required checks.

## Existing owner and reuse target (verified at `5db209cc`)

- Repo: `aiur-team/khala` (`git remote -v`). Workflow file `ci.yml`, workflow name `CI`, job `validate`.
- The visual baseline reproduction command is `ci.yml:56-61`.
- Vitest discovery uses the root `vitest.config.ts:11` `include: ['src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}']`. A `*.live.test.ts` (for example KM-110's `packages/agent/src/matrix/session.live.test.ts`) would therefore run in CI if its package did not exclude it; A10 requires the exclusion.

## Contract and invariants

No contracts.md shape is produced or consumed. A fix that would change any C1–C10 shape is out of scope: stop and ask the Executor.

**No test weakening.** None of the following is allowed:
- adding `.skip`, `.only`, `.todo`, `skipIf`, `--passWithNoTests` or `continue-on-error`;
- deleting or loosening an assertion, widening a regex or matcher, or lowering a count;
- raising a timeout more than 2× (state the measured reason);
- removing a CI step;
- deleting a test file. **Exception:** you may delete a test file when every module it tests was deleted by a merged M1 ticket. Cite the ticket and PR in the commit message.
- updating screenshot baselines. **Exception:** you may update them when the pixel change comes from a merged ticket that intentionally changed UI (cite it). Regenerate them only inside the pinned Playwright image.
- Live tests are the one structural exception. Per contracts C1 (reconciliation A10), `*.live.test.ts` files are excluded from each package's default `test` script and run only via `test:live` (KM-110 sets this up for `packages/agent`). If one still runs in CI and fails only because no stack is running, restore that exclusion and the `test:live` script in that package. The plan defines live tests as stack-only gates.

## Implementation pointers (refreshable @ 5db209cc)

### Files

Determined at pickup. Typical surfaces: the root `package.json`, package `package.json` scripts, adjacent `*.test.ts(x)` of code changed by a merged ticket, `scripts/check-*.mjs`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `apps/web/src/**/*-snapshots/`.

### Worked example

```
$ gh run list --repo aiur-team/khala --workflow ci.yml --branch main --status completed --limit 1 --json databaseId,headSha,conclusion
[{"databaseId":123456,"headSha":"abc1234...","conclusion":"failure"}]
$ gh run view 123456 --repo aiur-team/khala --log-failed | tail -60
validate  pnpm lint  scripts/check-boundaries.mjs: apps/web/src/x.ts: unresolved workspace import @khala/messaging/revocation/index
```

Fix: KM-120 left an import of a module KM-124 deleted. Remove the dead import in `apps/web/src/x.ts`, run `pnpm lint`, then commit `fix(ci): drop import of deleted revocation module (KM-124 #NNN)`.

### Steps

1. Pickup:
   1. `git fetch origin && git switch -c fix/ci-pass-1 origin/main`.
   2. Run the `gh run list` command from the worked example. Record the `databaseId` and `headSha` in the PR body.
   3. If `conclusion` is `success` and `headSha` equals `origin/main`, post that on the ticket and finish. No PR is needed.
2. `gh run view <id> --repo aiur-team/khala --log-failed > /tmp/ci-fail.log`. List each failing step and its first error.
3. Reproduce locally in CI order: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:browser`, `pnpm build`. For visual failures, use the `docker run` command from `ci.yml:56-59`.
4. Fix each failure at its root, smallest change first, one commit per root cause. Each commit message names the step and the ticket that caused it, if known.
5. Push and open a PR titled `fix(ci): repair main after M1 deletions (pass 1)`. The body contains the pickup run, a failure → cause → fix table, and the Non-goals list of later failures.
6. **Wait for CI:**
   1. `gh run list --repo aiur-team/khala --workflow ci.yml --branch fix/ci-pass-1 --limit 1 --json databaseId` gives the run ID.
   2. `gh run watch <id> --repo aiur-team/khala --exit-status`.
   3. If it fails, repeat Steps 2–6 on the PR run.

   Poll only through `gh run` (REST). Do not loop `gh pr view` or `gh pr checks`; they spend the shared GraphQL quota.
7. When `validate` is green, comment on the ticket with the green run URL. If the PR removes any file, state in the PR body that `deletion-guard` needs an admin approval on the head SHA. The reviewer handles it; do not push after asking for review.

## Test scenarios

The scenarios are the CI steps themselves.
1. `validate` on the PR's final head: every step green.
2. Local `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test && pnpm build` green on the same head.
3. `git diff origin/main...HEAD` contains no `.skip`, `.only`, `skipIf`, `continue-on-error` or removed `expect`/`assert` lines, except deletions allowed by Invariants. Check with `git diff origin/main...HEAD | grep -nE '^\+.*(\.skip|\.only|skipIf|continue-on-error)|^-.*(expect\(|assert)'` and justify each hit in the PR body.

## Verification

```sh
gh run watch <pr-run-id> --repo aiur-team/khala --exit-status   # exit 0
pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test && pnpm build
```

Done when the PR's `validate` run is green and its URL is on the ticket.

## Risks and stop conditions

- **Stop and report** (to the Executor, on the ticket) when a failure shows a real product regression whose fix is more than about 30 lines or changes behavior. Name the suspected merged ticket. The Executor may promote it as a `discovered_from` ticket (deferred-findings policy).
- **Stop** if green requires weakening a test under the rules above. Report the test and the reason.
- **Stop** if `main` keeps moving and new failures exceed the pickup scope by more than 3 distinct root causes. Finish the pickup scope and hand the rest to KM-161.
- Never force-push `main`, never change workflow triggers or required checks, and never retry a flaky step to green without a recorded cause.

## Complexity rationale

2: the work is unknown in size but bounded to diagnosing and making minimal fixes across known CI steps. Waiting for CI adds wall time, not difficulty.
